from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Two prisoners face a grid of sixty-four coins.", 
                         "One coin must be flipped to earn freedom.", 
                         "Can they coordinate a strategy for success?"]
        self.setup_layout("The Prisoner's Dilemma", lecture_lines)
        
        # Using SVG asset
        asset_path = "/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/prisoner.svg"
        alice = SVGMobject(asset_path).set_color("#FF0000")
        bob = SVGMobject(asset_path).set_color("#00FF00")
        alice_label = Text("Alice", font_size=20, color="#FF0000")
        bob_label = Text("Bob", font_size=20, color="#00FF00")
        
        # Grid representation (placeholder for the coins)
        grid_group = VGroup(*[Square(side_length=0.1, color=BLUE) for _ in range(8)])
        grid_group.arrange(RIGHT)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[0]))
        self.place_at_grid(alice, 'B3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(bob, 'B4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(alice_label, 'A3', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(bob_label, 'A4', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.place_in_area(grid_group, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(FadeIn(alice), FadeIn(bob), FadeIn(alice_label), FadeIn(bob_label), FadeIn(grid_group))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[1]))
        link = DashedLine(start=alice.get_center(), end=bob.get_center(), color="#FFFF00")
        self.play(Create(link))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[2]))
        self.play(Indicate(alice), Indicate(bob))
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Parity Principle", [
            "Parity tracks the state of a sequence.",
            "XOR operations determine if parity is even.",
            "Flipping one coin always reverses the parity."
        ])
        
        # Binary string: 1 0 1 1 0
        bits_str = "1 0 1 1 0"
        bits = VGroup(*[Text(c, font_size=36, color="#00FFFF") for c in bits_str.split()])
        bits.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.4)
        
        # Add Asset
        coin = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/coin.svg")
        coin.scale(0.3)
        coin_group = VGroup(bits, coin).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.5)
        
        # Fix 24: Move bits/coin up
        self.place_at_grid(coin_group, "B3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        bits_label = Text("Bits:", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        bits_label.next_to(coin_group, UP, buff=0.5)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"), Write(bits), Write(coin), Write(bits_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        xor_text = Text("1 ⊕ 0 ⊕ 1 ⊕ 1 ⊕ 0 = 1", font_size=28, color="#00FF00")
        # Fix 25: Move xor_text
        self.place_at_grid(xor_text, "C3", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(xor_text))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        
        # Highlight last bit and flip
        target_bit = bits[-1]
        self.play(Indicate(target_bit, color="#FF00FF"))
        
        new_bit = Text("1", font_size=36, color="#FF00FF") # Should be "0" -> "1"
        new_bit.move_to(target_bit)
        
        self.play(Transform(target_bit, new_bit))
        
        final_xor = Text("1 ⊕ 0 ⊕ 1 ⊕ 1 ⊕ 1 = 0", font_size=28, color="#FF00FF")
        # Fix 26: Move final_xor
        self.place_at_grid(final_xor, "D3", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(xor_text, final_xor))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Mapping Information to Geometry", [
            "Label every grid square with binary coordinates.",
            "The XOR sum of heads marks a square.",
            "Flipping that coin forces the board's parity."
        ])

            grid_lines.add(Line(self.grid["A1"] + np.array([-0.35, 0.35, 0]), self.grid["A6"] + np.array([0.35, 0.35, 0]) + [0, -i*0.7, 0], color=WHITE, stroke_width=1))
        
        # Assets
        coin = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/coin.svg")
        coin.set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Labels and Text
        binary_coords = Text("Binary: 00-11", font_size=16, color=WHITE)
        instructional_text = Text("XOR parity logic", font_size=18, color=GREY)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[0]))
        self.play(Create(grid_lines))
        self.place_at_grid(binary_coords, 'C5', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.add(binary_coords)
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[1]))
        self.place_at_grid(coin, 'B3', scale_factor=0.3)

        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)

        self.place_in_area(instructional_text, 'D1', 'F3', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.add(instructional_text)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion: Information Density", [
            "This strategy uses basic Hamming code principles.",
            "We encode information into simple parity checks.",
            "The grid becomes an error-correcting storage device."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        
        # Use asset: [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/grid.svg]
        # In this context, we will use SVGMobject or ImageMobject for the asset
        grid_asset = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/grid.svg")
        self.place_in_area(grid_asset, 'A3', 'F6', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.add(grid_asset)
        
        dots = VGroup(*[Dot(color="#00FFFF", radius=0.1) for _ in range(12)])
        grid_positions = [f"{r}{c}" for r in "ABCDEF" for c in "123456"]
        selected_positions = random.sample(grid_positions, 12)
        
        animations = []
        for i, dot in enumerate(dots):
            self.place_at_grid(dot, selected_positions[i])
            animations.append(FadeIn(dot))
        
        self.play(*animations)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        
        # Text for better explanation
        svm_explanation_text = Text("High Density Storage", font_size=20, color="#FF0000")
        self.place_in_area(svm_explanation_text, 'A1', 'B6', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # Red dots for high density
        red_dots = VGroup(*[Dot(color="#FF0000", radius=0.15) for _ in range(5)])
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(dots),
            FadeIn(svm_explanation_text),
            *[FadeIn(self.place_at_grid(red_dots[i], 'D4')) for i in range(5)]
        )
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Impossible Chessboard: Decoding Information Theory
outline.target_audience: University students with a basic interest in logic and computer science

sections.title: The Hook: The Prisoner's Dilemma
sections.content: Introduce the problem: A warden forces a prisoner to flip one coin on an 8x8 grid of 64 coins. A second prisoner must identify the specific coin flipped to earn freedom. Can they coordinate a strategy to guarantee success?
sections.example: Visualize a 64-square grid with random coins (Heads/Tails) and two agents: 'Alice the Observer' and 'Bob the Guesser'.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Parity Principle
sections.content: Explain the concept of 'Parity'—the idea that a sequence of bits can hold a 'checksum'. Introduce the XOR operation (0+0=0, 1+1=0, 0+1=1).
sections.example: A row of 3 coins: (H, T, H). Assign H=1, T=0. Sum = 1+0+1 = 2. The parity is 'Even' (0). Changing one coin flips the parity.

sections.title: Mapping Information to Geometry
sections.content: Assign each square on the chessboard a unique coordinate index from 0 to 63 (represented in binary: 000000 to 111111). We aim to make the XOR sum of all 'Heads' positions equal to the index of the square to be flipped.
sections.example: If the sum of all 'Heads' squares is 010111 (binary for 23), then the prisoner flips the coin at square 23 to force the board parity to match the target secret.

sections.title: The Mechanism: Decoding the Secret
sections.content: Explain how the second prisoner calculates the XOR sum of all 'Heads' squares on the board. The result tells them exactly which square the first prisoner changed.
sections.example: Visual animation: The board shifts from a random state to one where the XOR sum points precisely to the 'changed' coordinate, acting like a pointer.

sections.title: Conclusion: Information Density
sections.content: Summarize that this is an application of Hamming Codes. We have encoded 6 bits of information (the coordinate) into 64 bits of state, proving that information can be 'compressed' into parity checks.
sections.example: An analogy: Like a QR code, the entire board functions as a single error-correcting storage device where the 'error' is actually the message itself.
